parsed.explanation: Section 379 criminalises male-to-female gender presentation in public with up to 3 months' imprisonment, so outing can itself be an offence for a trans woman visitor. The same-sex statute was reported unenforced 2018-2022, and no Section 379 prosecution is sourced, which prevents a lower rating. Against that, security forces are reported to harass, arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ people in the same period, a minister threatened detention until procreation, a support group was raided and staff detained months without charge, there is no hate-crime or general anti-discrimination protection, no support organisations remain, and most openly LGBTQI+ citizens had fled hostile state rhetoric. State-perpetrated abuse with no remedy dominates the unenforced conduct statute.

entry_documents.exposure: Section 379 turns on public appearance alone; a mismatch between presentation and sex assigned/document may trigger questioning or arrest. No entry-screening practice documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/appearance discrepancy can convert a border or street check into investigation under the dress provision.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Security forces reported to harass, arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ persons 2018-2022; 2017 ministerial threat to detain until procreation; 2017 group raid with months' detention without charge.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest under dress or morality provisions can lead to the documented custody abuse; consular or legal remedy not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Section 379 criminalises gender presentation; unnatural-offence statute up to 10 years consensual remains on books; hostile official rhetoric and detention threat; NGO Act may bar supportive groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Only harassment protection noted is for oil and gas employees as of 2020, not a visitor protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile state framing licenses enforcement against visibly gender-nonconforming visitors despite reported non-enforcement of the conduct statute.

minors_guardians.interaction: No minor-specific rule documented; general dress and detention exposure would apply to a guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Widespread societal stigma reported; security forces themselves reported as perpetrators of harassment, beatings and torture, rather than protectors.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime or general anti-discrimination legislation for sexual orientation or gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Widespread stigma plus perpetrator police leaves a victim with no documented recourse, increasing street risk after outing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No known LGBTQ-support organisations; documented group closed after raid; most openly LGBTQI+ citizens fled; Section 379 enforcement itself undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of organisations, protection law, or documented remedy means an outed visitor has no identified channel to challenge detention or abuse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: dress-related criminalisation, repeated state detention/harassment, short statutory custody, no execution, weak remedy. This case rates slightly lower because torture/beating by security forces is documented, not only fines and brief detention.

Lower: 0.35-B has hours-long stops, fines and deference to police but no documented torture, procreation-detention threat, or flight of the openly LGBTQI+ population. Documented state abuse here is more severe.

Higher: 0.15-A has routine arrests, months of pretrial custody, common beatings and near-illusory appeals under an enforced decency regime. Here no Section 379 prosecution and no conduct-statute enforcement are reported 2018-2022, so that routine imprisonment pathway is not documented.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: nationwide dress criminalisation makes public presentation the trigger; reported non-enforcement of the conduct statute and absence of a sourced Section 379 prosecution keep the outcome from being routine imprisonment. However documented security-force harassment, detention, torture and beatings, a ministerial detention threat, closure of support infrastructure, hostile rhetoric and absence of any general protection make the state perpetrator rather than protector. Remedies, facilities, care and minor-specific rules are not documented and cannot be credited. The interaction is therefore arrest risk followed by abusive custody with no documented recourse.
